raw_case_text:
In 2014, a 35-year-old male resident of Rio de Janeiro was admitted with ulcerated lesions on his nasal septum, nasal cavity, palate, and balanopreputial sulcus (Figure 1). The patient had a past history of alcohol and cocaine abuse. The lesions initially appeared in 2013 as erythematous and painful papules that grew progressively larger. Additional symptoms included headache, nasal obstruction, asthenia, and weight loss. The initial differential diagnoses included MCL, paracoccidioidomycosis, neoplasia, granulomatosis with polyangiitis, and tuberculosis. The diagnosis of MCL was confirmed on the basis of positive IgG and IgM serology and histopathological examinations of the nasal mucosa and larynx. Nasal mucosa histopathological analysis showed dermal infiltration of histocytes, lymphocytes, and plasma cells in addition to some dilated vessels. The histopathologic analysis of the larynx showed extensive ulceration and inflammatory infiltrates, and a single macrophage with amastigote-like form in the cytoplasm. Videolaryngoscopy showed granulomatous and infiltrative lesions in the hypopharynx and larynx, hyperemia, and swollen vocal folds. There were also infiltrative lesions on the epiglottis, pyriform sinuses, and false folds. Results of viral and fungal serological tests, direct mycological examination, borehole azimuthal acoustic reflection imaging (BAAR), chest tomography, and respiratory function tests were all negative. Treatment with meglumine antimoniate was started but discontinued on day 22 due to phlebitis and fever. The patient was discharged on regression of all lesions and was referred for outpatient follow-up, but he did not return. He returned in 2018 because of recurrence and worsening of his condition. He presented with right-side nasal collapse and an erythematous lesion, which extended from the filter to the interior of the nasal orifice (Figure 2). Additionally, he had sinusitis with a foul-smelling discharge and blood clots. The sinus tomography showed nasal septum perforation and mucosal thickening of the maxillary sinus, with no other alterations on rhinoscopy. A 21-day treatment with intravenous amoxicillin/clavulanate was initiated.
Serology for leishmaniasis was IgG-positive and IgM-negative and non-reactive for paracoccidioidomycosis. Nasal mucosa histopathology showed ulcerated squamous mucosa with seromucous glands in the chorion. There were marked acute and chronic inflammatory processes with a giant cell reaction (Langhans cells) and epithelioid histocytes, compatible with a diagnosis of leishmaniasis (Figure 3). Nasal fragment polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis using the primer set 120 base pair detected leishmaniasis. However, PCR examination did not allow for species evaluation. The patient was administered amphotericin B treatment for 14 days, after which his lesions improved, and he was discharged. He was re-evaluated three months later with continued healing and was followed-up by our outpatient service.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 35-year-old male presented with chronic ulcerated lesions of the nasal septum, nasal cavity, palate, and balanopreputial sulcus, associated with nasal obstruction, headache, asthenia, and weight loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented in 2014 with painful ulcerated lesions of the nasal septum, palate, and balanopreputial sulcus that began in 2013 as erythematous papules, accompanied by headache, nasal blockage, asthenia, and weight loss. He received meglumine antimoniate for 22 days (discontinued due to phlebitis and fever) with lesion regression, but was lost to follow-up. In 2018, he returned with disease relapse manifesting as right-sided nasal collapse, an erythematous ulcer extending from the philtrum into the nasal cavity, and purulent sinusitis with blood clots. He was treated with intravenous amoxicillin/clavulanate for 21 days for acute bacterial sinusitis and admitted for definitive mucosal workup.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of chronic alcohol and cocaine abuse. Prior episode of mucocutaneous and genital ulcerations in 2014 partially treated with meglumine antimoniate. Resident of Rio de Janeiro, Brazil.
subjective.review_of_systems: Headache, nasal obstruction, asthenia, unintentional weight loss, foul-smelling purulent nasal discharge with blood clots. Home medications: amoxicillin/clavulanate IV. Allergies: None documented.

objective.physical_examination: Initial presentation (2014): ulcerated lesions on the nasal septum, nasal cavity, hard and soft palate, and balanopreputial sulcus. Relapse presentation (2018): right nasal wing collapse, extensive erythematous lesion extending from the philtrum to the interior of the nasal cavity, foul-smelling purulent nasal discharge with blood clots.
objective.routine_investigations: Microbiological and serological testing: Viral and fungal serologies negative; Paracoccidioidomycosis serology non-reactive; Direct mycological examination negative; Acid-fast bacillus smear (BAAR) negative; Respiratory function tests normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Videolaryngoscopy (2014): granulomatous and infiltrative lesions in the hypopharynx and larynx, marked hyperemia and swelling of vocal folds, and infiltrative lesions involving the epiglottis, pyriform sinuses, and false cords. Computed tomography: chest CT normal; sinus CT (2018) revealed nasal septum perforation and mucosal thickening of the maxillary sinus. Histopathology: 2014 nasal mucosa showed dermal infiltration by histiocytes, lymphocytes, and plasma cells with dilated vessels; larynx biopsy showed extensive ulceration and inflammatory infiltrates; 2018 nasal mucosa biopsy showed ulcerated squamous mucosa with marked acute and chronic inflammation, Langhans giant cells, and epithelioid histiocytes.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Relapsing mucocutaneous leishmaniasis (MCL) with destructive nasolaryngeal and genital mucosal involvement and nasal septal perforation.
Diagnostic confirmation: Leishmania serology was IgG-positive (positive IgG/IgM in 2014, positive IgG in 2018); 2014 laryngeal histopathology identified a macrophage with an intracellular amastigote-like form; 2018 repeat nasal biopsy demonstrated marked granulomatous inflammation with Langhans giant cells and epithelioid histiocytes compatible with leishmaniasis; 120-bp kinetoplast DNA PCR of nasal tissue was positive for Leishmania.
Differentials ruled out: Paracoccidioidomycosis (negative serology and direct mycological exam), tuberculosis (negative BAAR), syphilis, granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA), and mucosal squamous cell carcinoma.
Treatment and clinical course: Received intravenous amphotericin B for 14 days, resulting in prompt improvement and mucosal healing. Discharged with continued resolution verified at 3-month follow-up.
